note: Module Missing Message Fixer finds 'ghost' modules: rows in the key_value table, collection system.schema, whose name no longer resolves to an installed extension (extension.list.module getPathname throws). UI at /admin/config/system/module-missing-message-fixer (route module_missing_message_fixer.form, permission 'administer module missing message fixer'); Drush commands module-missing-message-fixer:list (alias mmmfl) and module-missing-message-fixer:fix (alias mmmff, name or --all). Fixing deletes the system.schema key_value row (and, via --all/UI, also <module>.* config). No config, no schema, no plugins. Medium/hard cases insert namespaced ghost schema rows (mmmf_*) into key_value collection system.schema and read/remove them; verify checks the row is gone.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal 11 site with module_missing_message_fixer installed, which Drush commands list and fix leftover 'missing module' entries, and what are their aliases?
evals.expected_output: drush module-missing-message-fixer:list (alias mmmfl) lists ghost modules; drush module-missing-message-fixer:fix <name> (alias mmmff), or with --all, removes them.

evals.prompt: What exactly is a 'missing module' that module_missing_message_fixer cleans up, and where is the stale record stored (which table and collection)?
evals.expected_output: A module whose code was removed from disk without a proper uninstall, leaving its schema version in the key_value table under the collection 'system.schema'. The fixer flags any system.schema name that no longer resolves to an installed extension.

evals.prompt: Where is the Module Missing Message Fixer admin page, what permission is required, and what does the 'Remove These Errors!' button actually delete?
evals.expected_output: Path /admin/config/system/module-missing-message-fixer (route module_missing_message_fixer.form), permission 'administer module missing message fixer'. Submitting deletes the selected names' rows from key_value (collection system.schema) and any <module>.* config objects.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site currently reports a leftover 'missing module' schema entry (a module whose files no longer exist). Using module_missing_message_fixer, inspect the live site and give the machine name of that ghost module.
evals.expected_output: The ghost module is mmmf_ghost: it has a row in key_value collection system.schema but no code on disk, so drush mmmfl (or the fixer UI) lists it.

evals.prompt: A stale module schema record has been left on this site for a module that is no longer present. Use module_missing_message_fixer's listing to identify and name the missing module (its machine name starts with 'mmmf_').
evals.expected_output: The missing module is mmmf_orphan, reported by drush mmmfl / the fixer because its system.schema key_value entry has no matching installed extension.

evals.prompt: This site has a ghost module schema entry named 'mmmf_task' (a system.schema key_value row for a module with no code). Using module_missing_message_fixer, remove that missing-module entry from the live site so it is no longer reported.
evals.expected_output: Remove the mmmf_task row from key_value collection system.schema, e.g. drush mmmff mmmf_task (or via the fixer UI). After fixing, \Drupal::keyValue('system.schema')->get('mmmf_task') is NULL.

evals.prompt: My Drupal site keeps warning about a missing module called 'mmmf_gone' that I already deleted. Make that warning go away by clearing the leftover record for mmmf_gone, using the Module Missing Message Fixer tool. Apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Clear the mmmf_gone system.schema entry (drush mmmff mmmf_gone, or select it in the fixer UI and Remove These Errors!). Afterwards \Drupal::keyValue('system.schema')->get('mmmf_gone') is NULL.
